official.deadline_note: No central EU student deadline exists. The European Commission states that in most cases applications are submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year, and that each master's own website has all the details of the application process; EACEA repeats that most master's programmes require applications between October and January for courses commencing the following academic year. Deadlines are set by each individual consortium, and some consortia run a separate scholarship deadline earlier than their admission deadline. For context, the institutional deadline for consortia applying for a new EMJM grant in the 2026 call (ERASMUS-EDU-2026-PEX-EMJM-MOB) was 12 February at 17:00 Brussels time - that date is for universities, not for students.
official.application_cycle: Annual, consortium-run rounds for the next academic year intake (the Commission: a new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the list each year, with applications in most cases between October and January for courses starting the following academic year). The underlying EMJM projects run for 6 academic years covering at least 4 editions of the master.
official.status_note: The scheme is open to students on a rolling annual cycle: the Commission states a new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the catalogue each year and that, in most cases, applications are submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year. EACEA currently lists 218 supported master's projects in the Erasmus Mundus Catalogue and warns that while many offer Erasmus Mundus scholarships, some do not because they are reaching the end of their funding period or hold only temporary use of the Erasmus Mundus name. The related institutional call for new EMJM grants (ERASMUS-EDU-2026-PEX-EMJM-MOB) closed on 12 February 2026, so the line-up of available tracks changes as new consortia are selected.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Erasmus+ student page states that scholarships 'cover your participation costs and contribute to travel, visa, a living allowance'. The Erasmus+ Programme Guide (Erasmus Mundus action, funding rules) states: 'Selected projects cannot charge student application fees. Moreover, projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders.'
benefits: Scholarship of EUR 1 400 per month, calculated on a monthly unit cost for the entire period needed to complete the programme: 'The scholarship is calculated as: 1 400 Euros/month x DS' (Programme Guide)
The scholarship covers travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs
Participation costs are covered: scholarship holders cannot be charged tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to participation in the course
A joint degree (one single certificate issued by at least two HEIs) or multiple degrees awarded by the consortium's institutions
Compulsory physical mobility in at least two countries, of which at least one must be an EU Member State or third country associated to the Programme

Special-needs support through unit-cost contributions from EUR 3 000 up to EUR 60 000 for enrolled students with disabilities, plus up to 18 NDICI-funded and up to 3 IPA III-funded additional scholarships for students from targeted regions of the world
eligibility: You must have a bachelor's degree (first degree), or be in your last year of bachelor studies
You must graduate before the master's programme starts
You may also apply if you demonstrate a bachelor's equivalent level of learning, officially recognised according to national legislation and practices in the degree-awarding country

Students from all over the world are welcome; EACEA confirms that for masters selected from 2021 the distinction between Programme and Partner countries no longer exists and all students receive the same scholarships
Students who have previously obtained an EMJM scholarship are not eligible to apply for an additional scholarship under the EMJM
Geographical balance applies: no more than 10% of the total number of scholarships awarded during project implementation should be awarded to candidates from the same nationality
requirements: Search the official Erasmus Mundus Catalogue for the latest selected programmes (218 projects currently listed)
Apply directly to the institution running the chosen programme, and contact the consortium for information on courses, application procedures and scholarship availability
Submit the application within the consortium's own deadline, in most cases between October and January for courses starting the following academic year
Be able to enrol on a full-time basis, as the scholarship is awarded for full-time enrolment only
Recognition of prior learning reduces the scholarship duration, with a minimum scholarship duration of one academic year
documents: The European Commission publishes no single central document list; the required documents are those listed on the chosen master's programme website
A bachelor's degree certificate, or proof of being in the last year of bachelor studies, or official evidence of a recognised equivalent level of learning
A Student Agreement signed by the enrolled student and the EMJM consortium upon enrolment (the template must be published on the programme's website)
A study agreement defining the joint or multiple degree route, signed with the consortium at the beginning of studies
Where individual-needs support is requested, enrolled students declare the type of items/services needed and their cost
selection_criteria: Masters may also offer full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide
Student selection must be organised transparently, impartially and equitably
The selection, recruitment and monitoring of individual students fall under the sole responsibility of the EMJM consortium
Consortia must ensure geographical balance in the award of scholarships (10% per-nationality cap)
coverage: Participation costs of the master's programme; projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders
Subsistence costs of EUR 1 400 per month, pro-rata of the actual number of days, for the entire period needed to complete the study programme (12, 18 or 24 months)
Full insurance coverage for enrolled students is included in the consortium's institutional cost unit
application_method: Search the Erasmus Mundus course catalogue on the EACEA website for the latest selected masters
Visit the programme's official website and contact the consortium directly for information on courses, application procedures and scholarship availability
Apply directly to the institution running the chosen programme, following the application steps published on that master's website (with and without scholarship)
Use the Erasmus Mundus Association resources (em-a.eu) for applicant advice, course contacts and national volunteer representatives
official.application_route: Apply directly to the consortium running the chosen Erasmus Mundus Joint Master through that programme's own published application system; there is no central EU application form, and the scholarship is decided inside the same consortium application.
official.study_mode: Full-time only - the scholarship can only be awarded in full, to full-time students, and covers the entire duration of the study programme
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality or residency restriction is published; students from all over the world are eligible. EACEA states that for masters selected from 2021 there is no distinction between Programme and Partner countries and all students receive the same scholarships.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to students from all over the world, with no nationality-based restriction; the only nationality rule is the balance requirement that no more than 10% of a project's scholarships go to candidates of the same nationality.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction at action level ('There is no limitation in terms of disciplines'); each consortium sets its own subject-background and entry requirements. Additional top-up scholarships are restricted to students from targeted regions of the world (regions 1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11).
official.research_requirement: The Commission states that Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters typically include periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence; admission requirements such as a research proposal are set by each consortium and published on its own website.
official.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits); the scholarship covers the entire duration of the programme, i.e. 12, 18 or 24 months
official.description: The Commission frames Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters as prestigious international masters, jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions, involving at least 3 institutions from at least 3 different countries and multiple associated partners, and states that full scholarships are available for the best students. Students from all over the world study in several countries and graduate with either a joint degree or multiple degrees.
official.region: Europe and beyond (at least 2 study periods in 2 countries, at least one of which must be an EU Member State or third country associated to the Programme). Belgium-scoped row: the Commission's own statistics show Belgium as a top-10 Erasmus Mundus country with 143 coordinator and full partner institutions (2004-2023), and EACEA's catalogue lists Belgian institutions including ULB among participating universities.
official.program_type: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) - integrated transnational master's programme leading to a joint or multiple degree (ISCED level 7)

not_confirmed: english_requirement - no English test score or medium-of-instruction rule is published by the European Commission; language requirements are set per consortium under the required joint language policy
deadline_date - no central deadline exists; each consortium sets its own application and scholarship deadlines
exact document lists - not published centrally, they are set and published by each consortium
per-programme scholarship quotas and payment schedule - not published centrally, they are fixed in each consortium's grant agreement and student pack

number of Belgian EMJM tracks currently offering scholarships for the 2027/2028 intake - the EACEA catalogue lists 218 projects but the country filter could not be narrowed to Belgium on the catalogue page during this check
verification.notes: The EUR 1 400 per month figure, its 24-month maximum and the tuition/travel/visa/installation/subsistence coverage were confirmed on three European Commission pages (Programme Guide Erasmus Mundus funding rules, the organisations page and the students page); EACEA pages supplied the catalogue status, the fee-fraud warning, the 2021 Programme/Partner country clarification and the Belgian institutional statistics.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no single Erasmus Mundus application and no single deadline: you shortlist masters in the EACEA catalogue, then file a separate application with each consortium, and the scholarship decision rides on that same consortium file. Budget against the EUR 1 400 monthly contribution rather than a guaranteed cost-of-living floor, because rent, flights, visa fees and deposits between two mandatory mobility countries stay with you. Treat October to January as your real submission window for the following academic year, and confirm on each programme's own site that scholarships are actually being awarded in that intake before you invest in the file.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year bachelor's students and recent graduates of any nationality with a strong transcript who want a two-country master's and can run several consortium applications in parallel during the autumn window.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist from the EACEA catalogue (218 listed projects) in September-October and verify on each programme's own website that Erasmus Mundus scholarships are still awarded for your intake, since EACEA warns some listed masters no longer award them
Build a tracker with each consortium's admission deadline and, where different, its separate scholarship deadline - they are not synchronised and some close early in the round
Secure the bachelor's certificate plus transcripts with certified translation; if you are still in your final year, obtain the official statement that you will graduate before the programme starts
Confirm you have never held an EMJM scholarship before, since previous holders are excluded from a second award
Prepare the specific language evidence each consortium names, and check passport validity plus visa lead times for your first obligatory mobility country
Email the consortium contact early to confirm scholarship availability and document format for your intake, and keep every confirmation in writing
common_rejection_risks: Missing the consortium's scholarship cut-off because it falls earlier than its admission deadline
Applying to a catalogue programme that no longer awards Erasmus Mundus scholarships in that edition
Failing the 10% per-nationality cap: large applicant cohorts from one country compete for very few places, so strong candidates are ranked out on balance grounds
Not graduating before the master's starts, which breaks the core eligibility rule and voids the award
Using an unrecognised equivalency claim instead of a properly recognised bachelor's equivalent level of learning
Submitting a file that fits a different programme's template instead of the named consortium's specific document list
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award is a contribution covering travel, visa, installation and EUR 1 400 per month, so you still fund housing deposits and first-month rent before money arrives, any shortfall between the allowance and local rents in both mobility cities, health insurance beyond the consortium's coverage, pre-application costs such as language tests and certified translations, and any individual-needs items below the EUR 3 000 special-needs threshold, which is not eligible for top-up support.
document_audit: Degree and transcripts must be in the form and language the consortium specifies; unofficial scans or missing certified translations stall the file
Name spellings must match across passport, degree certificate and application forms, and the passport must stay valid for the full visa process
The Student Agreement and study agreement are signed at enrolment and fix your joint-degree or multiple-degree route, so read them before signing rather than after
Language certificates must be the test the consortium names and still valid at the deadline
Keep evidence that you will graduate before the programme start, because final-year applicants are awarded conditionally on it
alerts: EACEA warns that EU scholarships are not granted for a fee and selected projects cannot charge student application fees - treat any payment request as fraud
The 2026 institutional call for new EMJM grants closed on 12 February 2026, so a track you saw advertised in an earlier year may disappear or change partners for the next intake

Belgium is a strong Erasmus Mundus host country (143 coordinator and full partner institutions, 2004-2023), and the catalogue's university filter lists KU Leuven, ULB, VUB, UCLouvain, ULiege, UMons, UNamur, Universiteit Antwerpen and Universiteit Gent - but participation in a consortium does not mean the Belgian semester is where you are based
The monthly allowance is paid by the consortium, and models differ (some offer advance travel/installation instalments that reduce the monthly amount), so check the payment terms before budgeting
The scholarship is full-time and covers the whole programme, so it cannot be stacked with a second EMJM award or used for part-time study
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Find the master's in the EACEA catalogue, open that consortium's own website, register in its application system, upload the required documents and motivation letter before its deadline, and the consortium's selection committee ranks candidates and allocates the limited scholarships itself.
